resources.title: NASA/JPL Horizons
resources.implementation: Bundled sampled positions and velocities set the moving gravity sources, date-specific injection states, trajectory predictions, live navigation, Earth range, and signal delay. Raw API responses, parameters, and hashes are included.
resources.contentUsed: Geometric Cartesian position/velocity vectors for eleven bodies, source GM values, query parameters and frame/time metadata.
resources.location: Horizons API vector tables; manifest body headers and parameters
resources.affectsGameplay: Yes: ephemeris positions, gravity, planning, navigation, Earth range and light time.
resources.testResult: Pass: retained date/range/interpolation, moving-gravity, navigation and communications tests; raw and binary hashes verified.
limitations: Bounded Hermite interpolation over the bundled 2025-01-01 to 2051-01-01 samples; launches limited to 2025-01-01 through 2030-12-31.
The existing point-mass multi-body model omits drag, radiation pressure and nonspherical gravity.
Selected interpolation fixtures are not a global error bound.

resources.title: Design and Develop Science Missions
resources.implementation: Existing measurable mission requirements now feed live readiness, a separate mission bonus, and saved flight reports. The full requirements trace remains available in offline research tools.
resources.affectsGameplay: Yes: existing requirement checks and measured science return affect mission scoring; report inspection itself gives no points.
resources.contentUsed: Four mission segments; science-to-requirements design process; ConOps validation; measurable requirements and verification planning.
resources.testResult: Pass: six requirements match ScienceOperations.report in four successful cases and one incompatible-instrument case.
limitations: A mission-design process adaptation; NASA does not supply the game hardware thresholds.
The existing game checks remain authoritative; the trace adds no score or success rule.

resources.title: NASA Goddard Mission Design Lab
resources.implementation: The existing tradeStudy function runs in a background Worker for configuration estimates. Measured battery reserve, fuel and data integrity inform the separate engineering score.
resources.location: Tailored Trade Study; MDL Capabilities; MDL Disciplines
resources.affectsGameplay: Configuration estimates are read-only; actual measured engineering outcomes affect the mission bonus. No NASA service is queried at runtime.
resources.contentUsed: Tailored studies of requirements and design alternatives across spacecraft disciplines, including mass, power, propulsion, communications and cost.
resources.testResult: Pass: eight instrument/radio alternatives per case; measured mass, delta-v, power, storage, radio and cost differences use shared game functions.
limitations: Hardware performance, prices and capacities are Educational Assumptions.
Alternatives are coast-only reference-track projections with no encounters, pickups or player thrust.
Resource rates use control seconds; projections are not full-duration energy-autonomy estimates.

resources.title: CubeSat 101
resources.implementation: Existing design requirements inform concise readiness and mission scoring. Detailed CubeSat accommodation and verification evidence remain in the offline review; game reserves and hardware values are educational assumptions.
resources.affectsGameplay: Existing mass, budget, instrument and lifetime checks affect mission completion and the bonus. The full CubeSat evidence review is offline and gives no extra points.
resources.contentUsed: Concept development, budget reserves, feasibility, design, mission coordination, documentation, ground communications, readiness reviews and operations.
resources.testResult: Pass: nine measured process checks, explicit hardware exclusions, and PDF/printed-page mapping verified.
limitations: Generic spacecraft, not a CubeSat-standard hardware design.
Dispenser dimensions, RF licenses, environmental qualification and flight certification are outside the simulation.
A 10% cost-reserve check follows the document recommendation when possible; it is advisory and uses the stated project denominator.

resources.title: Build It Yourself: A Learning Game About Telescopes
resources.implementation: Adapts its science-first design principle: each objective requires a matching measurement package. An incompatible instrument can still fly, but cannot satisfy the science mission. No source code or art was copied from this game.
resources.contentUsed: The educational workflow in which selected science drives compatible instruments and engineering choices.
resources.location: Build It Yourself introduction and Playing Hints
resources.affectsGameplay: Yes: existing objective/instrument compatibility and science-result checks; unchanged in 10.2.
resources.testResult: Pass: camera selection for the composition objective leaves physical arrival intact and fails the existing instrument/science checks.
limitations: Only the objective-to-measurement design workflow is adapted.
No telescope-game source code, assets, wavelength tables or optics model are reused.

resources.title: Space mission concept development using concept maturity levels
resources.implementation: Readiness and saved reports expose measured requirement results. The complete CML-informed evidence checklist remains in offline research tools; no official CML level is assigned.
resources.affectsGameplay: Read-only evidence organization; no additional grade or checklist-click bonus.
resources.contentUsed: Iterative concept development, early feasibility/trades, science data products, evidence checklists and the limits of assigning maturity levels.
resources.testResult: Pass: six evidence areas and unresolved risks use actual mission/trade data; officialCML remains null and the score is unchanged.
limitations: Simplified evidence checklist; the complete original CML matrix is not implemented.
No official maturity level, completeness threshold or independent review is claimed.

resources.title: NASA Image and Video Library / Hubble archives
resources.implementation: Successful flights unlock target-matched archived observations, retaining original image bytes, source URLs, credits, and SHA-256 hashes. They are not observations produced by the simulation.
resources.contentUsed: Six original NASA/partner archive renditions with image-specific source URLs, credits, file sizes and SHA-256 values.
resources.location: Image records: PIA13008, PIA12954, PIA00407, PIA02653 and two attributed Proxima Hubble observations
resources.affectsGameplay: Yes: the existing target-matched archive reward collection.
resources.testResult: Pass: original archive image bytes and credit/source records retained; six local image hashes verified.
limitations: Archive rewards are existing observations, not imagery produced by the simulated mission.
Source credits and original processing descriptions remain applicable.

resources.title: General Mission Analysis Tool (GMAT)
resources.implementation: A matched Earth point-mass benchmark script, local reference and comparison utility are supplied. GMAT R2025a was not available, so no independent GMAT result is claimed.
resources.contentUsed: NASA software catalog and R2025a release information used to prepare an optional matched-model benchmark.
resources.testResult: Not Executed: no GMAT executable or external output was available. Preparation and comparison-unit checks pass.
limitations: Script syntax and parameter assignments have not been validated by running GMAT.
The prepared benchmark uses Earth point-mass gravity only, not the live eleven-body model.
The synthetic offset test checks error calculations; it is not GMAT validation.

resources.title: NASA Mission Viz
resources.implementation: Tutorial-derived orbital elements are shown in expandable Trajectory Analysis using the actual departure state, origin, epoch and units. Full osculating-track exports remain available offline.
resources.location: Generate a flat surface ellipse; Transform the flat ellipse into a 3D orbit; Propagate a Keplerian orbit
resources.affectsGameplay: Read-only flight report analysis; it does not replace the 11-body trajectory, draw another orbit, change arrival, or award points.
resources.contentUsed: Focus-centered ellipse, sequential Y/Z/X rotation matrices, eccentric/mean anomalies and Keplerian timing from the tutorial.
resources.testResult: Pass: tutorial ellipse agrees with independently integrated two-body motion within 0.001 km; state/element round trips and Kepler residual tests pass.
limitations: Tutorial-derived Implementation; no NASA repository code copied because no applicable repository-wide license was established.
Classical Z/X/Z orbital elements are explicitly converted to the tutorial Y/Z/X orientation.
JSON/XYZ CSV are project-defined formats, not an official Mission Viz import API.
Osculating conics do not replace the live multi-body propagation; relativistic Proxima is excluded.

resources.title: Visualize a Space Mission Using Virtual Reality (2023)
resources.implementation: Background challenge reference. This release has no VR mode.
resources.contentUsed: The linked educational challenge description only.
limitations: No VR runtime, NASA VR software or VR data are used.

resources.title: Canadian Space Agency: Games and activities
resources.role: Partner learning resource; further study only
resources.implementation: Additional space learning activities. No CSA data are used in the calculations.
resources.contentUsed: The linked partner learning-resource collection only.
limitations: No CSA data, software or executable methods are used.

softwareReuse: No NASA repository source was copied. Mission Viz is a tutorial-derived independent implementation.
